## 1. Profile Overview

Yashasav is a software engineer working at the intersection of cutting-edge LLM inference, GPU kernel optimizations, and high-throughput distributed systems. His focus areas include:
- **LLM Inference Engine Internals**: FlashAttention SRAM tiling and Online Softmax mechanics, PagedAttention virtual KV block paging (vLLM), RadixAttention prefix-tree caching (SGLang), speculative decoding, chunked prefill, continuous batching, and KV cache compression.
- **GPU Architecture & CUDA**: Understanding compute- vs memory-bound operations, roofline models, HBM vs SRAM memory hierarchy (H100: 3.35 TB/s HBM vs 33 TB/s SRAM), warp-level parallelism, and IO-aware kernel design.
- **High-Throughput Distributed Systems**: Apache Kafka commit log internals, zero-copy `sendfile` I/O, log segment indexing, consumer lag management, and resilient inventory and fulfillment pipelines at Blinkit's quick-commerce scale.
- **Database Engineering**: PostgreSQL WAL and storage engine internals, Redis high-speed caching, RocksDB LSM-tree embedded storage, ACID guarantees.
- **Published Research**: Split federated learning and blockchain systems ("BloBS-FL", IEEE COMSNETS 2026).

## 2. Deep Dive: FlashAttention from First Principles

URL: https://kernel.yamuprajapati05.workers.dev/posts/flash-attention-deep-dive/

Standard attention is heavily memory-bandwidth bound on modern GPUs (like NVIDIA H100 with 3.35 TB/s HBM vs 33 TB/s SRAM).
Key concepts covered:
- **The Large N Memory Explosion**: Storing intermediate N×N score and probability matrices (S and P) requires over 524 GB across 32 heads at N=64k, instantly causing OOM on 80GB GPUs. The bottleneck is HBM read/write, not compute.
- **The Softmax Dilemma**: Naive block parallelization fails because softmax requires a global row-wise maximum and exponential sum to normalize—you can't split it across blocks without a second pass.
- **Online Softmax**: Mathematically rescales running max and exponential sums using e^(m_old - m_new), computing exact softmax over streaming chunks in a single fused kernel pass without materializing previous chunks to HBM.
- **2D SRAM Tiling (N=8, d=4 Walkthrough)**: Divides Q, K, V into SRAM-sized tiles, accumulates partial attention outputs in fast on-chip SRAM, and writes output tensor O to HBM exactly once. Intermediate weights S and P never touch HBM—achieving 3× speedups on standard benchmarks.

---

## 3. Deep Dive: Apache Kafka Internals - The Commit Log

URL: https://kernel.yamuprajapati05.workers.dev/posts/apache-kafka-internals-commit-log/

Kafka is fundamentally an append-only, immutable commit log persisted on disk, divided into partitions and segments.
Key concepts covered:
- **Sequential Disk I/O**: Kafka bypasses random disk access by appending records sequentially, achieving throughput comparable to network speeds (100MB/s+).
- **Page Cache & Zero-Copy (`sendfile`)**: OS page cache handles reads/writes. `sendfile` syscall transfers data from page cache to network socket without copying through user-space, eliminating two memory copies and two context switches per message.
- **Segment Files & Sparse Indexes**: Topics → partitions → segment files (`.log`). Offset indexes (`.index`) and timestamp indexes (`.timeindex`) enable O(log N) binary search for record retrieval without scanning the whole log.
- **Consumer Lag & Backpressure**: Consumers pull at their own pace based on committed offset vs log end offset (LEO). Backpressure is consumer-driven—the broker never pushes—enabling natural flow control across heterogeneous consumers.

---

## 4. Deep Dive: PagedAttention vs RadixAttention

URL: https://kernel.yamuprajapati05.workers.dev/posts/paged-attention-vs-radix-attention/

Memory management in LLM serving runtimes determines throughput and token generation efficiency.
Key concepts covered:
- **PagedAttention (vLLM)**: Solves external and internal KV cache memory fragmentation by dynamic virtual memory paging—allocates non-contiguous fixed-size block tables for KV tensors, mapping logical to physical pages like an OS virtual memory manager. Enables 2–4× higher batch sizes vs contiguous pre-allocation.
- **RadixAttention (SGLang)**: Solves prefix reuse across requests by maintaining KV cache blocks in a Radix Tree (trie) data structure. Allows rapid longest-prefix matching, automatic LRU eviction of cold sub-trees, and block sharing across system prompts, few-shot examples, and agent tool-call loops—achieving near-100% cache hit rates for multi-turn workloads.

## 5. Blog Post: AI Isn't Just Another Abstraction

URL: https://kernel.yamuprajapati05.workers.dev/posts/then-there-was-attention/

A first-principles argument for why LLM agents are not just the next level of tooling—they represent a qualitative architectural shift in how software is built. Covers:
- The 60+ year history of abstractions (Assembly → C → Python → Cloud/Kubernetes) and why the AI transition is fundamentally different in pace and kind.
- How LLMs store massive knowledge in numbers (bits-per-parameter capacity, 70B model ≈ 3–4× compressed English Wikipedia).
- Error compounding in multi-step agentic tasks and why CoT + tool-based verification loops are essential (0.95^20 ≈ 36% clean-run rate without checkpoints).
- The shift from engineer to architect: defining workflows, reviewing agent output, and maintaining evals and verifiers as first-class concerns.

## 6. Research Publication: BloBS-FL

Title: BloBS-FL: A Robust Architecture of Blockchain Based Decentralized Split Federated Learning
Publication: IEEE / COMSNETS 2026
URL: https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/abstract/document/11418208/

Overview:
Presents a robust decentralized architecture combining split federated learning with blockchain ledgers to eliminate single points of failure, prevent malicious gradient manipulation, and preserve data privacy in edge device model training.
